mainTopic: What רבי עקיבא asked רבי אליעזר about many מלאכות on many שבתות: the readings of רבה, אביי and רב חסדא, with their proofs
overview: The גמרא is working out exactly what רבי עקיבא asked רבי אליעזר about someone who did forbidden work on several שבתות. There are two cases. In שגגת שבת, he forgot it was שבת but knew the work was forbidden. In זדון שבת ושגגת מלאכות, he knew it was שבת but not that the work was forbidden. רבה says the first case was obvious to רבי עקיבא, because the weekdays in between split the sins. So the question was whether the שבתות count as separate 'bodies' in the second case. רבה proves this from the 'כלל גדול' משנה in מסכת שבת, which must follow רבי עקיבא. אביי disagrees: the second case was obvious (the שבתות are not separate), and the real question was whether the days in between split the sins. רב חסדא agrees with אביי about where the question lies, but holds that in the second case even רבי עקיבא treats each שבת separately. In all three readings, רבי עקיבא rejected רבי אליעזר's view that sub-labors count like main labors. רב חסדא then starts his proof from two ברייתות about writing two letters on two שבתות, and the proof continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Defining which case רבי עקיבא really asked about
steps.stepSummary: It is obvious that in שגגת שבת the days in between separate the sins, so רבי עקיבא's question must be about זדון שבת and שגגת מלאכות: are the שבתות like separate bodies?
steps.simpleTranslation: It makes sense to say this: in a case where he forgot it was שבת but knew the work was forbidden, it was obvious to רבי עקיבא that the weekdays in between count as awareness that splits the sins apart. What he asked about was the case where he knew it was שבת but did not know the work was forbidden: are the different שבתות treated like separate bodies, or not?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pins down exactly which case רבי עקיבא's question was about. One case is treated as obvious, and the question is placed on the other case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If a person forgets it is שבת, then during the weekdays in between he could learn of his mistake, so those days split the sins and each שבת brings its own חטאת. But if he knew it was שבת and only did not know the work was forbidden, the weekdays do not clear up his mistake at all. So the only way to split the שבתות is if each שבת counts as a separate 'body', a separate unit of sin. That is the question.

keyTerms.meaning: It stands to reason; it makes sense
Doing work by mistake because he forgot that the day is שבת
Knowing that the kinds of work are forbidden on שבת
The weekdays between one שבת and the next
Awareness that splits sins into separate units, so each needs its own קרבן
They are like separate 'bodies', separate units that each bring their own קרבן

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two cases. 'שגגת שבת' means he forgot what day it was. 'שגגת מלאכות' means he knew it was שבת but did not know the work was forbidden. The weekdays in between only help in the first case.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets the frame for the whole discussion. The question is not about the days in between. It is about whether each שבת counts as its own unit of sin.

steps.mimraCoreRuling: In שגגת שבת the weekdays in between separate the sins, and this is obvious. רבי עקיבא's question was only about זדון שבת and שגגת מלאכות: are the שבתות like separate bodies?

steps.title: רבי אליעזר answers that the שבתות are separate units, but רבי עקיבא does not accept it
steps.stepSummary: רבי אליעזר ruled that in זדון שבת and שגגת מלאכות each שבת counts as a separate body. רבי עקיבא did not accept this.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אליעזר answered him that when a person knows it is שבת but does not know the work is forbidden, the שבתות are like separate bodies. But רבי עקיבא did not accept this from him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא reports רבי אליעזר's answer to the question from step 1, and tells us that רבי עקיבא rejected it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אליעזר holds that each שבת is its own unit of sin, so the person would bring a separate חטאת for each שבת even though no awareness came in between. רבי עקיבא disagrees. In his view, without awareness in between, the separate שבתות do not split the sin.

keyTerms.meaning: He solved the question for him; he gave him an answer

Knowing that the day is שבת
Not knowing that the kinds of work are forbidden on שבת

steps.title: רבי אליעזר answers that sub-labors count like main labors, but רבי עקיבא does not accept it
steps.stepSummary: For רבי עקיבא's second question, רבי אליעזר ruled that sub-categories of work count like the main categories. Again רבי עקיבא did not accept this.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי אליעזר answered him that the offshoots of the labors are like the main labors. But רבי עקיבא did not accept this from him either.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא reports רבי אליעזר's answer to רבי עקיבא's other question, and once again רבי עקיבא rejects it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question was whether a sub-category of forbidden work, done together with its main category, counts as a separate act that needs its own חטאת. רבי אליעזר says yes, it counts just like a main labor, so there is a separate חטאת for each. רבי עקיבא disagrees here too.

keyTerms.meaning: Offshoots of the labors: sub-categories that come from the main categories of forbidden work
They are treated like the main labors

steps.whatToRemember: רבי אליעזר answered both questions in favor of separate חטאות: each שבת counts on its own, and each sub-labor counts on its own. רבי עקיבא accepted neither answer.

steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Sub-labors count like main labors and bring separate חטאות. רבי עקיבא rejected this.

steps.title: רבה brings the 'great principle' משנה: one who forgets שבת entirely brings one חטאת
steps.stepSummary: רבה supports his reading from the משנה in מסכת שבת. Someone who forgot the very idea of שבת and did much work on many שבתות brings only one חטאת.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה said: How do I know this? Because we learned in a משנה: They said a great principle about שבת. Anyone who forgets the basic idea of שבת, and did many labors on many שבתות, owes only one חטאת.
steps.whatsHappening: רבה begins proving the reading he gave in step 1, using a well-known משנה. This step quotes the first case of that משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In this first case, the person does not know that שבת exists at all. Since he never knew, nothing during the weekdays could make him realize his mistake. So all his sins come from one single lapse, and he brings just one חטאת. This is the starting point that the next two cases are built on.

keyTerms.meaning: From where do I say this? An opening that introduces a proof
A great, broad principle
One who forgets the very essence of שבת, not knowing work is forbidden on שבת at all
He is liable for only one קרבן חטאת

phrases.english: Rabba said: From where do I say this?
As we learned in a mishna,
They stated a great principle regarding Shabbat:
Anyone who forgets the essence of Shabbat,
and performed many labors

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבָּה מְנָא אָמֵינָא לַהּ דִּתְנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to step 1 and begins bringing a source to support רבה's reading.
steps.raayaObject: רבה's claim from step 1 that in שגגת שבת the weekdays in between obviously separate the sins.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The 'כלל גדול' משנה in מסכת שבת 67b.

steps.title: The משנה's other two cases: a חטאת for each שבת, or a חטאת for each main labor
steps.stepSummary: Someone who knows about שבת but forgot the day was שבת brings a חטאת for each שבת. Someone who knows it is שבת but not that the work is forbidden brings a חטאת for each main labor.
steps.simpleTranslation: One who knows the basic idea of שבת, and did many labors on many שבתות, owes a חטאת for every single שבת. One who knows that it is שבת, and did many labors on many שבתות, owes a חטאת for every single main category of labor.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes quoting the משנה that רבה brought as his proof. These are its second and third cases.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The second case is שגגת שבת: he knows שבת is forbidden but lost track of the days. Here the משנה says he brings a חטאת for each שבת, and that is because the weekdays in between give him awareness that separates the sins, just as step 1 said is obvious. The third case is שגגת מלאכות: he knows it is שבת but not that the work is forbidden. Here the count goes by main labor, not by שבת.

keyTerms.meaning: One who knows the basic idea of שבת, but forgot which day is שבת
For each and every שבת separately
One who knows that today is שבת, but does not know the work is forbidden
A main category of forbidden work on שבת

steps.whatToRemember: The three levels in the משנה: forgot שבת entirely means one חטאת; forgot the day means one חטאת per שבת; forgot the forbidden labors means one חטאת per main labor. רבה uses the middle case to show that in שגגת שבת the weekdays in between clearly separate the sins.
steps.confusionAlert: 'יודע עיקר שבת' and 'יודע שהוא שבת' sound alike but mean different things. The first person knows שבת exists but forgot what day it is. The second knows today is שבת but does not know the work is forbidden.

steps.title: The משנה does not count each שבת separately in the third case
steps.stepSummary: רבה points out what the משנה leaves out. In the case of knowing it is שבת but not that the work is forbidden, it does not say 'liable for each main labor of each שבת'. So there the שבתות are not counted separately.
steps.simpleTranslation: But the משנה does not say 'he is liable for each main labor on each and every שבת.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבה is reading the משנה closely and noticing what it does not say. This sets up the question of whose opinion the משנה follows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the case of זדון שבת ושגגת מלאכות, the משנה counts only main labors, not the separate שבתות. So in that case, doing the same labor on many שבתות still brings just one חטאת for that labor. This is the opposite of רבי אליעזר's answer to רבי עקיבא's first question.

steps.title: Whose view is this משנה? Not רבי אליעזר
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks who wrote this משנה. It cannot be רבי אליעזר, because the end of the משנה says many sub-labors of one main labor bring only one חטאת. רבי אליעזר holds that each sub-labor counts on its own.
steps.simpleTranslation: Whose view is this? If you say רבי אליעזר, look at the end of the משנה: one who does many labors that all belong to one main labor brings only one חטאת. But if it were רבי אליעזר, he would be liable for every sub-labor as if it were a main labor!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks whose opinion the משנה follows. It immediately rules out רבי אליעזר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 3, רבי אליעזר ruled that sub-labors count like main labors. The end of this משנה says the opposite, so the משנה cannot be his. That leaves רבי עקיבא, which the next step will use.

If you would say

phrases.english: he would be liable for every sub-labor like main labors!
phrases.notes: This is רבי אליעזר's ruling from step 3.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַנִּי הָא? אִילֵימָא רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר, אֵימָא סֵיפָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Identifies the author of the משנה just analyzed, so the proof can be applied to רבי עקיבא.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Not רבי אליעזר, since the סיפא contradicts his ruling on sub-labors

steps.title: It is רבי עקיבא, and he already held that the days in between split the sins
steps.stepSummary: So the משנה is רבי עקיבא's. Since it gives a חטאת for each שבת in שגגת שבת, רבי עקיבא clearly held that the days in between split the sins there.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it is obviously רבי עקיבא. Learn from this: in שגגת שבת וזדון מלאכות, it was obvious to him that the days in between count as knowing, and they split the sins apart.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא concludes that the משנה follows רבי עקיבא. From that it learns what he already held in the case of forgetting it was שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה (step 5) gives a חטאת for each שבת when he forgot the day was שבת. Since this is רבי עקיבא's משנה, he had no doubt about that case. The weekdays between each שבת act like a moment of knowing that separates the sins.

Learn from it

The days in between (the weekdays between one שבת and the next)
Knowing that splits the sins into separate חטאות

steps.confusionAlert: Keep the two cases straight. שגגת שבת means he forgot it was שבת but knew the work was forbidden. זדון שבת means he knew it was שבת but did not know the work was forbidden.

and learn from it

that the days in between count as knowing, to separate the sins,

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא פְּשִׁיטָא רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא הִיא, וּשְׁמַע מִינַּהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 7 and draws the first inference about רבי עקיבא.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רבי עקיבא, who therefore held that the days in between split the sins in שגגת שבת

steps.title: So רבי עקיבא's question was about זדון שבת, and he rejected both answers
steps.stepSummary: רבי עקיבא's doubt must have been about זדון שבת ושגגת מלאכות: are the שבתות like separate bodies? רבי אליעזר said yes, and that sub-labors count like main labors. רבי עקיבא accepted neither answer, exactly as the משנה shows.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was in the case of knowing it is שבת but not knowing the labors are forbidden that he asked whether the שבתות are like separate bodies. רבי אליעזר answered that they are like separate bodies, and that sub-labors are like main labors. רבי עקיבא accepted neither answer from him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא wraps up רבה's proof. It confirms his reading from step 1: the question was only about זדון שבת ושגגת מלאכות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The case of שגגת שבת was already clear to רבי עקיבא (step 8), so his doubt must have been in the other case. The משנה follows רבי עקיבא. It does not count separate שבתות in the זדון שבת case, and its last clause does not count separate sub-labors. So he rejected both of רבי אליעזר's rulings.

keyTerms.meaning: He knew it was שבת but did not know the labors are forbidden
They are like separate bodies (each one counts on its own)
He resolved the question for him
He did not accept it from him

steps.whatToRemember: רבה proves from the משנה that רבי עקיבא's doubt was only about זדון שבת ושגגת מלאכות. In שגגת שבת, he agreed that each שבת gets its own חטאת. In זדון שבת, he rejected רבי אליעזר's view on both separate שבתות and sub-labors.
steps.whyThisMatters: Under this reading, the משנה in מסכת שבת fits רבי עקיבא's view in both cases.

phrases.english: It is about knowing it is שבת but mistaking the labors
that he asked whether they are like separate bodies,
and he resolved it for him that they are like separate bodies,
and sub-labors are like main labors,
and he did not accept either of them from him.

steps.triggerLanguage: זְדוֹן שַׁבָּת וְשִׁגְגַת מְלָאכוֹת הוּא דְּבָעֵי אִי כְּגוּפִין דָּמְיָין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the final conclusion from step 8, confirming the reading of steps 1-3.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: רבי עקיבא's question was about זדון שבת ושגגת מלאכות. רבי אליעזר said separate שבתות and sub-labors each count, and רבי עקיבא rejected both, as the משנה in מסכת שבת shows.

steps.title: אביי: the doubt was about forgetting it is שבת, not about forgetting the labors
steps.stepSummary: אביי rejects רבה's reading. For רבי עקיבא, זדון שבת ושגגת מלאכות was obvious: the שבתות are not separate bodies. His real question was about שגגת שבת וזדון מלאכות: do the days in between act as יְדִיעָה (awareness) that splits the sins?
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to him: Really, I can tell you that in the case of knowing it is שבת but not knowing the labors are forbidden, it was obvious to רבי עקיבא that the שבתות are not like separate bodies. What he asked about was the case of forgetting it is שבת while knowing the labors are forbidden: do the days in between count as awareness that divides the sins, or not?
steps.whatsHappening: אביי rejects רבה's conclusion from step 9. He moves רבי עקיבא's doubt to the other case, שגגת שבת וזדון מלאכות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבה said רבי עקיבא was unsure whether the שבתות count like separate bodies in זדון שבת ושגגת מלאכות. אביי says that was never a doubt: the משנה's silence there shows the plain view that they do not count separately. The question was something else: when a person forgets it is שבת, do the weekdays in between give him a kind of awareness that splits one שבת's sin from the next?

keyTerms.meaning: "Really, I can tell you": the opener for rejecting someone's proof by offering another reading
He knows it is שבת but does not know these labors are forbidden
He forgot it is שבת but knows these labors are forbidden
"They are like separate bodies": each one counts as its own unit for a separate חטאת
The weekdays between one שבת and the next
Awareness that splits sins, so each part needs its own חטאת

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up the two cases. In זדון שבת the person knows the day but not the law. In שגגת שבת the person knows the law but forgot the day. אביי is moving the doubt from the first case to the second.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ אַבָּיֵי: לְעוֹלָם אֵימָא לָךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects רבה's conclusion in step 9 about which case רבי עקיבא's doubt concerned.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects רבה's identification of רבי עקיבא's doubt as being about זדון שבת ושגגת מלאכות.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The משנה's wording in that case does not show a doubt; it simply shows that רבי עקיבא held the שבתות are not separate bodies there. The doubt can be placed in the other case.

steps.title: אביי: what רבי אליעזר answered and what רבי עקיבא accepted
steps.stepSummary: In אביי's reading, רבי אליעזר answered that the days in between do split the sins, and רבי עקיבא accepted this. רבי אליעזר also said sub-labors count like main labors, but רבי עקיבא did not accept that.
steps.simpleTranslation: And he resolved it for him: the days in between count as awareness to divide, and he accepted it from him. And he also resolved for him that sub-labors are like main labors, but he did not accept it from him.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי finishes his version of the story. He shows which of רבי אליעזר's answers רבי עקיבא took and which he turned down.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This fits the משנה. In שגגת שבת the משנה gives a חטאת for each שבת, which matches accepting that the days in between split the sins. The end of the משנה gives only one חטאת for many sub-labors of one main labor, which matches rejecting רבי אליעזר's view on sub-labors.

keyTerms.meaning: He resolved the question for him
He accepted it from him
Sub-labors: acts that come from one of the main labors (אבות מלאכה)

steps.whatToRemember: According to אביי: in שגגת שבת the days in between split the sins, and רבי עקיבא agreed. In זדון שבת the שבתות do not count separately. Sub-labors do not count separately from their main labor, which is רבי עקיבא's view against רבי אליעזר.

phrases.english: And he resolved it for him
phrases.notes: רבי אליעזר is answering רבי עקיבא.

phrases.english: that the days in between count as awareness to divide

and he resolved for him

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes אביי's reading by giving רבי אליעזר's answers and רבי עקיבא's responses.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The days in between split the sins (accepted). Sub-labors count like main labors (not accepted).

steps.title: רב חסדא: even רבי עקיבא counts the שבתות separately when the labors are forgotten
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא disagrees with אביי about זדון שבת ושגגת מלאכות. He says even רבי עקיבא holds the שבתות are like separate bodies there. He agrees, though, that the question to רבי אליעזר was about שגגת שבת and the days in between.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חסדא said: In the case of knowing it is שבת but not knowing the labors are forbidden, even רבי עקיבא holds that they are like separate bodies. When he asked him, it was about forgetting it is שבת while knowing the labors are forbidden that he asked: do the days in between count as awareness to divide?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second reading, from רב חסדא. It treats the case of זדון שבת differently from אביי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי said that in זדון שבת ושגגת מלאכות it was obvious the שבתות are NOT separate bodies. רב חסדא says the opposite: even רבי עקיבא agrees they ARE separate bodies there. Both agree that the actual question was about שגגת שבת and the days in between.

keyTerms.meaning: Even: here, even רבי עקיבא, who might have been expected to disagree
He holds (this view)

steps.confusionAlert: אביי and רב חסדא agree about which case the question was about. They disagree only about the other case, זדון שבת ושגגת מלאכות.

phrases.english: Rav Chisda said:

even Rabbi Akiva holds
that they are like separate bodies,
and when he asked him,

phrases.english: it was about forgetting it is Shabbat while knowing the labors are forbidden that he asked him,

phrases.aramaic: דְּיָמִים שֶׁבֵּינְתַיִים אִי הָוְיָין יְדִיעָה לְחַלֵּק.
phrases.english: whether the days in between count as awareness to divide.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב חִסְדָּא אָמַר: זְדוֹן שַׁבָּת וְשִׁגְגַת מְלָאכוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a different reading from אביי's, reversing his view on זדון שבת ושגגת מלאכות.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In זדון שבת ושגגת מלאכות even רבי עקיבא counts each שבת separately. The question to רבי אליעזר was about whether the days in between split the sins in שגגת שבת.

steps.title: רב חסדא: רבי עקיבא accepted that the days in between split the sins
steps.stepSummary: In רב חסדא's reading, רבי אליעזר answered that the days in between split the sins, and רבי עקיבא accepted it.
steps.simpleTranslation: And he resolved it for him: the days in between count as awareness to divide, and he accepted it from him.
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא finishes his version. רבי עקיבא accepted רבי אליעזר's answer about the days in between.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This matches the משנה, which gives a חטאת for each שבת in שגגת שבת. The next step adds רבי אליעזר's second answer in רב חסדא's reading, about sub-labors.

keyTerms.meaning: They count as awareness

steps.whatToRemember: Both אביי and רב חסדא agree: in שגגת שבת, the days in between split the sins, so each שבת needs its own חטאת. They disagree only about זדון שבת ושגגת מלאכות.

phrases.english: And he resolved it for him
the days in between count as awareness to divide,
and he accepted it from him.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּפְשַׁיט לֵיהּ יָמִים שֶׁבֵּינְתַיִים הָוַיִין יְדִיעָה לְחַלֵּק
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes רב חסדא's reading with רבי אליעזר's answer and רבי עקיבא's acceptance.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The days in between count as awareness that splits the sins, and רבי עקיבא accepted this.

steps.title: Sub-labors count like main labors, but רבי עקיבא rejects it
steps.stepSummary: In רב חסדא's reading, רבי אליעזר also answered that sub-labors (תולדות) count like main labors. רבי עקיבא did not accept this answer.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי אליעזר also answered him that sub-labors are like main labors, but רבי עקיבא did not accept it from him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes laying out the exchange between רבי אליעזר and רבי עקיבא according to רב חסדא. רבי אליעזר gave a second answer, and רבי עקיבא rejected it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 13 gave the answer רבי עקיבא accepted: the days in between split the sins. This line adds the second answer, that sub-labors count separately like main labors, which רבי עקיבא did not accept. This matches the picture in אביי's reading in Step 11.

keyTerms.meaning: Sub-labors: actions that come from one of the main forbidden labors of שבת (also called תּוֹלָדוֹת)
He answered (solved) the question for him
He did not accept the answer from him

steps.whatToRemember: In רב חסדא's reading, רבי עקיבא accepted one answer (the days in between split the sins) and rejected the other (sub-labors count like main labors).

phrases.english: And he answered him that sub-labors

but he did not accept it from him.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּפְשַׁט לֵיהּ דְּוַלְדֵי מְלָאכוֹת כִּמְלָאכוֹת דָּמַיִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the second half of רבי אליעזר's answer in רב חסדא's reading.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Sub-labors count like main labors, but רבי עקיבא did not accept this.

steps.title: רב חסדא brings his source: the first ברייתא about writing two letters
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא asks where he learns his view and quotes a ברייתא. Writing two letters in one lapse of awareness makes a person חייב. With two lapses, רבן גמליאל says חייב and חכמים say פטור. But רבן גמליאל agrees that one letter on one שבת and one letter on another שבת is פטור.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חסדא said: From where do I say this? As a ברייתא teaches: Someone who writes two letters in one lapse of awareness is חייב. In two lapses of awareness, רבן גמליאל says חייב and the חכמים say פטור. And רבן גמליאל agrees that if he wrote one letter on this שבת and one letter on another שבת, he is פטור.
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא starts proving his view that, in זדון שבת ושגגת מלאכות, even רבי עקיבא treats each שבת as a separate body. This step only brings the first source; the proof itself comes in the next steps.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Writing two letters is the smallest amount of writing that makes someone חייב. If both letters are written in one lapse, they join together. With two lapses, רבן גמליאל still joins them, but with two different שבתות even he says the letters do not join, so the person is פטור.

keyTerms.meaning: From where do I say this? (introduces a speaker's own source)
One lapse of awareness: one stretch of forgetting, with no remembering in between
Two letters: the minimum amount of writing that makes one חייב on שבת
Agrees: the one who disagrees admits this case

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב חִסְדָּא: מְנָא אָמֵינָא לַהּ?

phrases.notes: "It" is his view that in זדון שבת ושגגת מלאכות even רבי עקיבא treats each שבת as separate (Step 12).

In two lapses of awareness:

And Rabban Gamliel agrees that if he wrote
one letter on this Shabbat

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב חִסְדָּא: מְנָא אָמֵינָא לַהּ? דְּתַנְיָא

steps.raayaObject: רב חסדא's claim that in זדון שבת ושגגת מלאכות even רבי עקיבא treats the שבתות as separate bodies.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא: רבן גמליאל agrees that one letter on each of two שבתות is פטור.

steps.title: A second ברייתא seems to say the opposite about רבן גמליאל
steps.stepSummary: Another ברייתא says that for two letters on two שבתות, רבן גמליאל says חייב and חכמים say פטור. So the two ברייתות seem to contradict each other. The גמרא assumes רבן גמליאל holds like רבי עקיבא.
steps.simpleTranslation: And another ברייתא teaches: Someone who writes two letters on two שבתות, one on this שבת and one on that שבת, רבן גמליאל says חייב and the חכמים say פטור. You might think that רבן גמליאל holds like רבי עקיבא.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second ברייתא that clashes with the first one about רבן גמליאל. This sets up the next step, where רב חסדא shows that his view solves the clash.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first ברייתא says רבן גמליאל agrees two שבתות means פטור. The second says he holds חייב in that same kind of case. Since רבן גמליאל is assumed to follow רבי עקיבא, a good reading of רבי עקיבא must explain both ברייתות.

keyTerms.meaning: You might think: an assumption the גמרא is working with for now
He holds (this opinion)
Holds liable / hold exempt

steps.confusionAlert: Both ברייתות talk about two letters on two different שבתות, yet they give opposite rulings for רבן גמליאל. The answer will be that they are talking about different kinds of mistakes.

phrases.english: And it is taught in another baraita:
One who writes two letters on two Shabbatot,

phrases.aramaic: אֶחָד בְּשַׁבָּת זוֹ וְאֶחָד בְּשַׁבָּת זוֹ –

phrases.english: that Rabban Gamliel holds like Rabbi Akiva.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a second ברייתא that seems to contradict the first.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ruling of רבן גמליאל in the first ברייתא.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: One ברייתא has רבן גמליאל saying פטור for letters on two שבתות, and the other has him saying חייב.
steps.raayaObject: רב חסדא's claim that in זדון שבת ושגגת מלאכות even רבי עקיבא treats the שבתות as separate bodies.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A second ברייתא in which רבן גמליאל holds חייב for one letter on each of two שבתות, set against the first ברייתא where he agrees it is פטור.

steps.title: רב חסדא: my view explains the ברייתא that says פטור
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא says his view works well. Since even רבי עקיבא holds that in זדון שבת ושגגת מלאכות the שבתות are separate bodies, the ברייתא that says פטור is talking about that case.
steps.simpleTranslation: This works well according to me, since I say that in זדון שבת ושגגת מלאכות even רבי עקיבא holds that the שבתות are like separate bodies. So the ברייתא that says פטור is talking about זדון שבת ושגגת מלאכות, where the שבתות are like separate bodies.
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא starts solving the contradiction using his own view. He places the פטור ברייתא in the case of זדון שבת ושגגת מלאכות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If each שבת is a separate body, a letter on one שבת cannot join a letter on another שבת to reach the two-letter minimum, so the person is פטור. This explains the first ברייתא even for רבן גמליאל, who follows רבי עקיבא. The other ברייתא (חייב) will need to be about a different case.

keyTerms.meaning: It works well according to me: opens an argument that only one view can explain a source
He knows it is שבת but does not know these actions are forbidden labors
Are like separate bodies: each counts on its own and does not join with the others

steps.whyThisMatters: "בשלמא לדידי" sets up a proof: רב חסדא's view can explain both ברייתות, which suggests the other view (אביי's) will have trouble doing so.

steps.raayaObject: רב חסדא's view that in זדון שבת ושגגת מלאכות even רבי עקיבא treats the שבתות as separate bodies.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The פטור ruling in the first ברייתא fits the case of זדון שבת ושגגת מלאכות.
